definitions.explanation: A formal or semi-formal statement expressing willingness to do something, making a request, or putting forward a proposal. Derived from the verb 申し出る (to offer, to propose). Used in business and official contexts.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{申|もう}し{出|で}を{受|う}け{入|い}れた。
ボランティアの{申|もう}し{出|で}が{多数|たすう}{寄|よ}せられた。
examples.english: Numerous offers to volunteer were received.

examples.japanese: {退職|たいしょく}の{申|もう}し{出|で}は、{少|すく}なくとも{一|いっ}か{月|げつ}{前|まえ}までに{上司|じょうし}に{伝|つた}えてください。
examples.english: Please inform your supervisor of your resignation request at least one month in advance.

notes:
USAGE:
A formal noun derived from the verb {申|もう}し{出|で}る. Used to refer to offers, proposals, and requests in business, administrative, and official settings.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {申|もう}し{出|で}を{受|う}ける (receive an offer)
- {申|もう}し{出|で}を{受|う}け{入|い}れる (accept an offer)
- {申|もう}し{出|で}を{断|ことわ}る (decline an offer)
- {退職|たいしょく}の{申|もう}し{出|で} (resignation request)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {提案|ていあん}: proposal, suggestion (more about ideas or plans)
- {申請|しんせい}: application, formal request (more bureaucratic, involves paperwork)
- {申|もう}し{込|こ}み: application, entry (specifically for registering or signing up for something)
